title: An organic badge, addresses in Google Maps, and planting by trade unit
summary: Organic producers are easy to spot, addresses open in Google Maps, and planting acres count under the trade unit you choose.

items.text: Organic producers now show an Organic Producer badge next to their name. Click it to see their NOP ID.
Click a producer's address to open it in Google Maps. The address now includes the ZIP code.
Trade unit names now come from Trade Unit Preferences, so they match the names set there instead of an older list that could be out of date.

When you add a planting intention you now choose which of the producer's trade units it is for, and the dashboard counts those acres only there. A producer on two trade units no longer has their acres counted under both.

The producer's planting table now has a Trade Unit column in place of Created On, and you can move a row to another trade unit when you edit it. Entries made before this release for producers on two trade units may be on the wrong one, so check those rows.
When you remove a producer from a trade unit that has planting intentions, you are asked where those acres should count instead.

Grain on farm is now recorded by specific commodity, such as HRWW or SRWW, using the same list as planting intentions. Existing entries keep their crop group, such as Wheat, until you edit them and pick the commodity.

title: Follow-ups, Teams channels, and lists that follow your trade units
summary: Set your own reminders on a producer, send a note straight to a Teams channel, and find your saved lists where you expect them.

items.text: You can set a follow-up on a producer and see it on their page under My Follow-Ups. These are private to you, and nobody else can see them.
Each follow-up also goes on your Outlook calendar, with a reminder the day before, so you get a nudge without having to come back into the app.

A producer with a follow-up coming up shows a clock on the producer list, colour-coded by how soon it is due. Build a List has a new Follow-Ups Scheduled card that pulls up everyone you owe a follow-up.

Typing @ in a note now offers the Teams channels you belong to, as well as people. Pick one and the note is posted straight to that channel. A channel only appears in the list if it has an email address set up in Teams — open the channel, choose Get email address, and it will show up here.

A Daily Recap group can be pointed at a Teams channel instead of email. Mention that group in a note and it posts to the channel rather than mailing everyone. Set it up under Manage Groups, using the channel email address.

A saved list now shows up whenever any one of its trade units is selected, instead of only when your selection matched exactly. Lists saved across two trade units used to disappear when you looked at one of them on its own.
Re-saving a list while a different trade unit was selected could permanently drop producers you had added by hand. Those producers are now kept.

The Crops filter now lists specific commodity codes rather than broad crop groups, so you can separate HRWW from SRWW instead of getting all wheat at once. You can still narrow by state in the same panel.

Organic and identity-preserved crops now show under their own names, such as Organic Soybeans and Waxy Corn, instead of being counted as the conventional crop. This applies to the Planting Intentions dashboard, the producer's planting table and the print report, and their acres and coverage are now measured against their own contracts. Existing entries pick this up on their own.
After each release the app tells you what changed, once. You can reopen it any time from the What's New row in your profile menu.
Your profile menu now shows which release and build you are on. Quote that line when you report a problem and we can tell exactly what you were running.
